topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under RCW 18.85.241, how does the statute set the fee a designated broker must pay to establish a branch office?
choice_a: The fee is prescribed by the director through administrative rule, not fixed as a dollar amount in the statute itself
choice_b: The statute fixes the fee at exactly $500
choice_c: No fee is ever required to establish a branch office
choice_d: The fee is set annually by the county auditor where the branch is located
explanation: RCW 18.85.241 grants branch office authority "upon the payment of a fee as prescribed by the director by rule" -- the statute delegates the actual fee-setting to administrative rule rather than fixing an amount in the RCW text.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under RCW 18.85.241, a properly authorized branch office must be established under what name?
choice_a: The same name as the real estate firm
choice_b: Any name the branch manager personally selects
choice_c: A name distinct from the firm, chosen to distinguish each branch location
choice_d: The name of the building's property manager
explanation: RCW 18.85.241 authorizes a designated broker to establish one or more branch offices "under the same name as the real estate firm" -- a branch office is not a separately named entity.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under RCW 18.85.241, the 35-mile branch-office exception applies specifically to what kind of activity?
choice_a: Real estate sales activity that is conducted on, and limited to, a particular subdivision or tract
choice_b: General brokerage activity conducted anywhere within the same county
choice_c: Property management activity only, regardless of location
choice_d: Activity conducted entirely online with no physical presence anywhere
explanation: The 35-mile exception applies only where sales activity "is conducted on and, limited to a particular subdivision or tract" -- it does not exempt general brokerage operations spread across a wider area.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under RCW 18.85.241, is a designated broker limited to establishing a single branch office?
choice_a: No, the statute allows a designated broker to apply for authority to establish one or more branch offices
choice_b: Yes, a firm is capped at exactly one branch office statewide
choice_c: Yes, additional branches require a separate act of the legislature
choice_d: No, but only if each additional branch is in a different county
explanation: RCW 18.85.241 lets a designated broker apply for authority to establish "one or more branch offices," so firms are not limited to a single branch location.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under RCW 18.85.231, besides being accessible to the director's representatives, what must a firm's office or records depository contain?
choice_a: A complete set of records as required under the chapter
choice_b: A notarized copy of every client's driver's license
choice_c: A copy of every competing firm's price list
choice_d: Nothing beyond a valid mailing address
explanation: RCW 18.85.231 requires the office or records depository to be accessible to representatives of the director and to hold a complete set of records as required elsewhere in the chapter.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under RCW 18.85.231, who has authority to establish rules governing alternative and electronic methods of record storage for real estate firms?
choice_a: The director
choice_b: Each individual county's licensing office
choice_c: The firm's outside CPA
choice_d: The federal Consumer Financial Protection Bureau
explanation: RCW 18.85.231 retains for the director the authority to adopt rules governing alternative and electronic methods of record storage, which the department later implemented through WAC 308-124C-110.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under RCW 18.85.221, apart from the assumed-name option, what does a real estate license NOT authorize a licensee to do?
choice_a: Operate in any manner other than under the name appearing on the license
choice_b: Hire unlicensed staff for purely clerical work
choice_c: Advertise using the licensee's own middle name
choice_d: Complete continuing education courses online
explanation: RCW 18.85.221 states that no license authorizes any person other than the one named on it to act under it, "nor to operate in any other manner than under the name appearing on the license," apart from a properly licensed assumed name.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under RCW 18.85.221, is a real estate firm required to adopt an assumed name?
choice_a: No, adopting an assumed name is optional -- the firm "has the option" to use one or more assumed names
choice_b: Yes, every licensed firm must adopt at least one assumed name
choice_c: Assumed names are permitted only for branch offices, never for the main firm
choice_d: Only sole proprietorships may ever use an assumed name
explanation: RCW 18.85.221 gives a firm "the option to utilize one or more assumed names" -- it is a permissive choice, not a mandatory requirement, though each assumed name used must be separately licensed.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under RCW 18.85.091, a firm license applicant must designate a managing broker to serve in what role, with what authority?
choice_a: As the firm's "designated broker," with authority to act for the firm
choice_b: As the firm's bookkeeper, with authority limited to payroll matters
choice_c: As a silent partner with no operational authority
choice_d: As an at-will employee holding no fiduciary role
explanation: RCW 18.85.091 requires a firm license applicant to designate a managing broker as the "designated broker," who has authority to act for the firm.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under RCW 18.85.091, what disqualifies a person from holding a controlling interest in a licensed real estate firm?
choice_a: Being the subject of a final departmental order suspending or revoking any type of real estate license
choice_b: Having more than ten years of general business experience
choice_c: Living outside the state of Washington
choice_d: Holding an active real estate license issued by another state
explanation: RCW 18.85.091 bars a person from holding a controlling interest in a firm if that person is or has been the subject of a final departmental order suspending or revoking any type of real estate license.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under RCW 18.85.091, what restriction applies to the name a real estate firm may adopt for licensure?
choice_a: It cannot be the same or similar to a currently issued license, and cannot imply nonprofit status or government affiliation
choice_b: It must include the designated broker's full legal name
choice_c: It must be a single word of no more than eight characters
choice_d: There is no restriction on the firm name a firm may adopt
explanation: RCW 18.85.091 prohibits a firm from adopting a name that is the same as or similar to a currently issued license, or a name implying nonprofit status or a governmental affiliation the firm does not have.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under RCW 18.85.091, a firm license application must include a Washington business mailing and street address, a contact telephone number, and what else?
choice_a: A physical address for the firm's trust account or business records
choice_b: The personal home address of every affiliated broker
choice_c: A five-year business plan for department review
choice_d: A letter of reference from a competing real estate firm
explanation: Among its application requirements, RCW 18.85.091 requires a physical address where the firm's trust account or business records are kept, in addition to the firm's mailing/street address and phone number.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under RCW 18.85.091, upon renewal a licensed firm must notify the director of changes in what two areas?
choice_a: Controlling interest and secretary of state filings
choice_b: Employee parking arrangements and office decor
choice_c: The firm's advertising budget and marketing vendor
choice_d: The firm's insurance carrier only
explanation: RCW 18.85.091 requires a firm, at renewal, to submit notice of any changes in controlling interest and any changes in its secretary of state filings, along with the renewal fee.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under RCW 18.85.255, who must give written notice to the director of a change in business or records depository location?
choice_a: A designated broker, managing broker, or firm
choice_b: Only unlicensed clerical staff at the office
choice_c: The county recorder for the new office's location
choice_d: The buyer in the licensee's most recently closed transaction
explanation: RCW 18.85.255 requires a designated broker, managing broker, or firm to give written notice to the director of any change to that licensee's business or records depository location.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under RCW 18.85.255, what must happen before the director issues a replacement license reflecting a new office location?
choice_a: The original license must be surrendered and the required fee paid
choice_b: The old office must remain vacant for 90 days
choice_c: A public hearing on the relocation must be held
choice_d: The firm must close and reopen under a new business name
explanation: RCW 18.85.255 provides that upon surrender of the original license and payment of the required fee, the director must issue a replacement license reflecting the new location.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124C-105, what receipt-related record must a designated broker maintain for trust account funds?
choice_a: A duplicate receipt book or cash receipts journal recording all receipts
choice_b: A single annual receipt summary submitted to the department
choice_c: Verbal confirmation logs kept by the front-desk assistant
choice_d: No receipt record is required if the client pays by check
explanation: WAC 308-124C-105 requires the designated broker to maintain a duplicate receipt book or cash receipts journal recording all receipts of trust funds.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124C-105, what check-related records must a designated broker maintain for trust account disbursements?
choice_a: Sequentially numbered, nonduplicative checks along with a check register, cash disbursements journal, or check stubs
choice_b: A photograph of every check written from the account
choice_c: Only the bank's monthly statement, with no internal register
choice_d: Checks may be handwritten with no numbering system required
explanation: WAC 308-124C-105 requires sequentially numbered, nonduplicative checks paired with a check register, cash disbursements journal, or check stubs documenting trust account disbursements.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124C-105, what deposit documentation must a designated broker maintain for the trust account?
choice_a: Validated duplicate bank deposit slips, or a daily verified bank deposit record
choice_b: A notarized affidavit for each individual deposit
choice_c: No deposit documentation is required as long as reconciliation is current
choice_d: Only the client's verbal confirmation that a deposit was made
explanation: WAC 308-124C-105 requires validated duplicate bank deposit slips or a daily verified bank deposit as part of the required trust account records.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124C-105, beyond ledgers for ordinary real estate sale transactions, what other types of accounts require a client accounting ledger?
choice_a: Property management accounts, contracts, and mortgage collection accounts
choice_b: The firm's own internal payroll account
choice_c: The designated broker's personal retirement account
choice_d: No other account types require a client ledger
explanation: WAC 308-124C-105 requires a client accounting ledger documenting monies received and disbursed not only for sale transactions but also for property management accounts, contracts, and mortgage collection accounts.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124C-105, may a firm use an automated system instead of handwritten ledger sheets for each tenant, lessee, vendee, or mortgagor?
choice_a: Yes, automated systems may generate computer printouts in place of handwritten ledger sheets
choice_b: No, only handwritten ledger sheets satisfy the requirement
choice_c: Only if the department pre-approves the specific software used
choice_d: Automated systems are permitted only for firms with fewer than five licensees
explanation: WAC 308-124C-105 permits automated recordkeeping systems to use computer-generated printouts in lieu of manually maintained separate ledger sheets.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124C-105, what log must a designated broker maintain regarding brokerage service agreements or contracts submitted by affiliated licensees?
choice_a: An accurate, current log of all such agreements or contracts
choice_b: A log required only for agreements exceeding $1 million in value
choice_c: No log is required if the contracts are stored electronically
choice_d: A log limited only to agreements that were later canceled
explanation: WAC 308-124C-105 requires the designated broker to maintain an accurate, current log of all brokerage service agreements or contracts submitted by affiliated licensees.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124C-105, what must a designated broker retain in firm files for each transaction or brokerage service contract?
choice_a: A legible copy of each transaction or brokerage service contract
choice_b: Only a one-paragraph internal summary of the deal
choice_c: Nothing; the client retains the sole surviving copy
choice_d: A copy only when the transaction failed to close
explanation: WAC 308-124C-105 requires a legible copy of each transaction or brokerage service contract to be retained in the firm's files.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124C-110(1), what three standards must all required real estate records meet?
choice_a: They must be accurate, posted, and kept up to date
choice_b: They must be typed, notarized, and produced bilingually
choice_c: They must be color-coded by transaction type
choice_d: They must be reviewed quarterly by an outside auditor
explanation: WAC 308-124C-110(1) states that all required real estate records shall be accurate, posted, and kept up to date.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124C-110, when closed transaction records are stored at a central Washington facility rather than at the licensed office, what must the licensed office itself maintain?
choice_a: A complete listing of all transactions stored remotely
choice_b: Nothing further; the licensed office has no ongoing obligation
choice_c: A duplicate paper copy of every remotely stored record regardless
choice_d: A public notice posted in the office lobby describing the facility
explanation: Even when closed records over a year old are stored at a central facility, WAC 308-124C-110 requires the licensed office to maintain a complete listing of all transactions stored there.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124C-110, a firm using electronic or remote record storage must maintain what at the licensed office location itself?
choice_a: Functioning equipment capable of immediately retrieving, viewing, and printing the stored documents
choice_b: A dedicated server room open for public tours
choice_c: A fireproof safe containing paper backups only, with no electronic access
choice_d: Nothing; the equipment may be located anywhere in the country
explanation: WAC 308-124C-110 conditions electronic or remote storage on the firm maintaining functioning equipment at the licensed location, with the capability to immediately view and print the stored documents.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124C-110, how must an electronic or remote storage system be organized?
choice_a: Indexed so that documents can be immediately retrieved upon the department's demand
choice_b: Organized alphabetically by the client's first name only
choice_c: There is no particular indexing requirement
choice_d: Sorted exclusively by the dollar amount of each transaction
explanation: WAC 308-124C-110 requires the storage system to be indexed so records can be immediately retrieved for the department upon demand.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124C-115, the 20-day notification clock for a reportable event begins running from what triggering point?
choice_a: Service of the relevant document, or the licensee's knowledge of the event, whichever applies first
choice_b: Only the date a final court judgment is entered, regardless of any earlier knowledge
choice_c: The date the licensee's personal attorney formally advises them of the matter
choice_d: The start of the licensee's next license renewal cycle
explanation: WAC 308-124C-115 requires notification within twenty days "after service or knowledge thereof," so the clock can start running from either service of process or the licensee's actual knowledge of the event.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124C-130, in addition to making firm offices and records accessible to the director's authorized representatives, what else must a branch manager provide upon demand?
choice_a: Required copies of records
choice_b: A written apology letter regarding any complaint
choice_c: A list of every client's personal phone number
choice_d: Nothing further is required of the branch manager
explanation: WAC 308-124C-130 requires a branch manager to make the firm's offices and records accessible to the director's authorized representatives and to provide required copies of records upon demand.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124C-130, what must a branch manager verify about everyone employed by, contracted with, or representing the branch office?
choice_a: That they hold appropriate licenses for the services they perform
choice_b: That they hold a four-year college degree
choice_c: That they reside within the branch office's ZIP code
choice_d: That they personally own their own vehicle
explanation: WAC 308-124C-130 requires the branch manager to verify that all persons employed, contracted with, or representing the branch office hold appropriate licenses.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124C-130, what personnel actions fall within a branch manager's responsibilities for branch licensees?
choice_a: Hiring, transferring, and releasing branch licensees
choice_b: Setting each branch licensee's personal income tax withholding
choice_c: Approving branch licensees' personal home mortgage applications
choice_d: Nothing; personnel decisions rest solely with the designated broker
explanation: WAC 308-124C-130 makes the branch manager responsible for the hiring, transferring, and releasing of branch licensees.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124C-130, a branch manager must cooperate with the department during what kinds of proceedings?
choice_a: Investigations, audits, or licensing matters
choice_b: Only criminal trials involving the firm's designated broker
choice_c: City council meetings addressing local zoning
choice_d: Federal tax audits of the branch manager personally
explanation: WAC 308-124C-130 requires the branch manager to cooperate with the department during investigations, audits, or licensing matters, the same duty imposed on designated and managing brokers.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124C-130, a branch manager must maintain competency regarding which statutes and rules?
choice_a: Chapters 18.85, 18.86, and 18.235 RCW, and the rules adopted under them
choice_b: Local property tax assessment methods
choice_c: Federal securities law
choice_d: Building code inspection standards
explanation: WAC 308-124C-130 requires the branch manager to maintain competency regarding the applicable statutes -- chapters 18.85, 18.86, and 18.235 RCW -- and the rules promulgated under them.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124B-200, how does the license-display requirement for an individual broker differ from that for firm and branch office licenses?
choice_a: An individual license must be available at the address appearing on the license, while firm and branch office licenses must be displayed in an area visible to the public
choice_b: Both types must be mailed to the department every month
choice_c: Individual licenses must be publicly displayed, while firm licenses may be kept private
choice_d: Neither type of license carries any location or display requirement
explanation: WAC 308-124B-200 distinguishes the two: individual broker and managing broker licenses need only be available at the address on the license, while firm and branch office licenses must be displayed where the public can see them.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124B-205, besides the completed change of address application, what must the designated broker submit within the 10-day window?
choice_a: The return of all licenses, completed transfer applications, and payment of the correct fees
choice_b: A notarized letter from the new office's landlord
choice_c: Nothing further; the application form alone is sufficient
choice_d: A new business plan for the relocated office
explanation: WAC 308-124B-205 requires the designated broker to submit the change of address application together with the return of all licenses, completed transfer applications, and payment of the correct fees, within 10 days.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: Under WAC 308-124B-207, the required firm or assumed-name identification must be displayed at what specific location?
choice_a: The address appearing on the license
choice_b: Any address the firm chooses, regardless of what the license shows
choice_c: The firm's corporate headquarters only, even if that is out of state
choice_d: The branch manager's personal residence
explanation: WAC 308-124B-207 requires the licensed firm name or assumed name to be displayed, visible to the public, "at the address appearing on the license."

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: According to the Department of Licensing, a real estate branch office must share what identifying number with its parent firm?
choice_a: The firm's Unified Business Identifier (UBI) number
choice_b: The designated broker's Social Security number
choice_c: A separate UBI number unique to the branch itself
choice_d: The branch manager's individual license number
explanation: Per Department of Licensing guidance, a branch office must be established with the same Unified Business Identifier (UBI) number as the parent firm, under the firm's name.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: According to the Department of Licensing, how many branch locations may a single managing broker or designated broker manage as branch manager at the same time?
choice_a: Only one branch location
choice_b: Up to five branch locations
choice_c: An unlimited number, as long as each is properly delegated in writing
choice_d: Two branch locations, but only within the same county
explanation: Department of Licensing guidance states that managing brokers and designated brokers can each be a branch manager of only one branch at a time.
source_note: DOL: Get your license - Real estate branch office (dol.wa.gov)

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: According to the Department of Licensing, who applies for a new real estate branch office license through the SecureAccess Washington (SAW) online system?
choice_a: The designated broker or an administrator
choice_b: The prospective branch manager alone, without firm involvement
choice_c: Any individual broker affiliated with the firm
choice_d: The department itself initiates the application on the firm's behalf
explanation: Department of Licensing guidance directs the designated broker or an administrator to submit the branch office application online through SecureAccess Washington (SAW), or by mail as an alternative.
source_note: DOL: Get your license - Real estate branch office (dol.wa.gov)

topic: WA Managing Broker: Branch Office Supervision & Recordkeeping
question: According to the Department of Licensing, what form is used to endorse a managing broker as the branch manager for a new branch office?
choice_a: The Real Estate Endorsement Application
choice_b: The Real Estate Firm Application
choice_c: A simple notarized letter, with no formal application required
choice_d: The Continuing Education Provider Application
explanation: Department of Licensing guidance requires the Real Estate Endorsement Application to be submitted for the managing broker being endorsed as the branch office's branch manager.
source_note: DOL: Get your license - Real estate branch office (dol.wa.gov)
